segment_text: (c) Each Service Recipient and its respective Service Provider shall cooperate in good faith with each other in connection with the performance of the Services hereunder. Each of TWX and Time, in its capacity as a Service Provider, agrees to appoint one of its respective employees (each such employee, a “Service Manager”) who will have overall responsibility for managing and coordinating the delivery of Services, including making available the services of appropriately qualified employees and resources to enable the provision of the Services. The Service Managers will consult and coordinate with each other regarding the provision of Services.

annotator_notes:
S2 of E01-004 -- the SECOND of the segment's two items.

SEGMENT SHAPE. E01-004, 3 sentences, all three modal-bearing, 2 obligation-bearing clauses -- within section 2's 1-3 band. S1 [0:170] and S2 [171:548] are the two items. S3 [549:650] is NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING, and that is settled by the DOCUMENT'S OWN DEFINITIONAL TEXT rather than by inference: E01 defines "Service Manager" INSIDE S2 -- 'appoint one of its respective EMPLOYEES (each such employee, a "Service Manager")' -- so S3's subject 'The Service Managers' is a set of EMPLOYEES, not contracting parties. That is section 3.5 / section 8.8's non-party-subject class, and E07-010's exact ground ('These personnel shall also be responsible for the installation of new TIBCO software releases'), which already fires on a LOCKED segment. Verified by reading E01's own definitions list, which routes "Service Manager" to Section 2.01(c) -- this very sentence. Because S3 is not an item, the fact that 'coordinate' has no taxonomy member never arises.

A REGISTRY-COMPLETENESS GAP FOUND IN PASSING, NOT LOAD-BEARING HERE AND RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED. E01 defines "Service Provider" (78 occurrences) and "Service Recipient" (57) as QUOTED, DEFINED ROLES, and section 21 R3 requires a registry to carry 'every party the source document's own preamble defines, PROPER NAMES AND DEFINED ROLES ALIKE'. evals/registry/E01.json carries only TWX -> Time Warner Inc. and Time -> Time Inc. NOTHING IN THIS SEGMENT TURNS ON IT: both items are underspecified on section 3.9 trigger 1 regardless, because both obligor values are distributive/collective references that resolve_party() could not match whatever the registry held. Belongs with CLAUDE.md's registry debt bullet (filed 2026-09-24).

MODALITY MUST, AND IT IS NOT A JUDGMENT CALL. 'agrees to' is an explicit row in section 3.2's modality table, so this does not go through the 'will'-ambiguity rule at all. (The sentence's other modal, 'who WILL have overall responsibility', sits inside a relative clause describing the appointee and governs nothing the obligor is told to do.)

ACTION APPOINT, a literal taxonomy member. SINGLETON ACCEPT-SET on ordinary section 3.4 grounds, NOT section 8.8's -- no tag is owed, because APPOINT is the verb the sentence uses. WHY IT CANNOT WIDEN IS WORTH STATING, because section 8.8 names two obvious candidates: 'nominate' and 'designate' are listed there as DEFENSIBLY MAPPABLE to APPOINT -- but NEITHER IS A TAXONOMY MEMBER, and section 3.4 admits only taxonomy verbs into a gold accept-set (section 5.1 A1's inertness finding, and the drafting hazard flagged at v0.53). A mapping running INTO a member does not make the mapped-from verb an accept-set entry. No other member is defensible.

OBLIGEE ABSENT. The appointment runs to nobody named in the span -- 'Service Recipient' does not appear in S2 at all. Section 3.5's ordinary positional test; section 3.5.4 is cited because obligee assignment does not turn on modality.

NO MUTUAL_OBLIGATION, AND THE OPPOSITE RESULT TO THIS SEGMENT'S OTHER ITEM IS THE PROCEDURE WORKING. Section 8.4.2 in order: (a) MUST, PASSES. (b) 'Each of TWX and Time' is a distributive naming both parties, PASSES. (c) the obligee is that same counterparty: NO obligee is stated, and (c)'s own text rules that 'obligee: ABSENT is a FAILURE, not a deferral'. FAILS. Same outcome and same failing test as C04-02. E01-04, one sentence earlier with the same two parties, DOES carry the tag because it says 'with each other'; the discrimination is exactly what section 8.4.2 was written to make.

NO COMPOUND_ACTION, checked rather than assumed because the sentence contains four further verb forms. 'managing and coordinating' and 'making available' all sit INSIDE THE RELATIVE CLAUSE DESCRIBING THE APPOINTEE'S RESPONSIBILITY, not in the obligor's commanded act. The only thing TWX and Time are told to do is APPOINT. This is the same prior-filter logic section 8.8.4 states as its filter 3 -- where a construction is the CONTENT of another predicate it states nothing about the obligor's own duty -- whose worked case is C04-117 sitting inside locked item C04-02's own span.

OBJECT_CLASS 'service_manager'. Head noun of the object phrase ('one of its respective EMPLOYEES') is 'employee', carried as the head-only member section 3.6's v0.58 forward rule requires -- and it is the head noun OF THE OBJECT PHRASE, the bound C04-03's counter-example exists to enforce. The slot itself is 'service_manager' because that is THE DOCUMENT'S OWN WORD FOR THE OBJECT, defined parenthetically in this very sentence -- section 3.6.1's carve-out 1, whose precedent is C22-01's 'notice'. SECTION 3.6.1 CLEAR: no member restates the action or either party ('Service Manager' names the appointee role, not the obligor's 'Service Provider' capacity). 'appointed_employee' and 'designated_employee' were DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED -- both restate APPOINT.

CONDITIONS EMPTY. 'in its capacity as a Service Provider' fails section 3.8.2's removal test: delete it and the duty applies in exactly the same circumstances. It qualifies WHICH HAT the obligor wears, not WHETHER the obligation applies -- scope, not a gate.

TEMPORAL NULL. No timing phrase.

UNDERSPECIFIED TRUE on section 3.9 trigger 1, twice: 'Each of TWX and Time' is a DISTRIBUTIVE reference, named explicitly by that trigger -- and note it would NOT resolve even though 'TWX' and 'Time' are each individually registry-resolvable in evals/registry/E01.json, because resolve_party() matches an alias string and the slot value is the whole distributive phrase; and obligee is ABSENT.

KNOWN_GAPS EMPTY, WHICH IS WORTH STATING RATHER THAN PASSING OVER: this item ENTERS section 9.1's kind-scoped in-force criterion-2 denominator. It is the ONLY one of batch 5's six items to do so other than C10-03 -- and C10-03 is there only because F25's gap class has no tag yet, whereas this item is there because it genuinely carries no gap. C10-025 and E01-004 both lack cassettes, so both are cassette-unscoreable today and report.py's G8 discloses them.

PROVENANCE. As for E01-04 above: pool rebuild gate, byte-for-byte match against draw.json, gated sentence splitter.
